cmad.notes: CMAD expected for operational NASA mission but not located. Parker Solar Probe is operating (no StopDate) and NASA-funded (Living With a Star, contract NNN06AA01C), and the mission's own Science Data Management Plan (Rev B, September 2021, section 2.2.2) states that 'All projects need a Calibration and Measurement Algorithm Document ... a project-level document and maintained publicly at the NASA archives'. Searched: (a) no designated CMAD repository is configured; Zenodo searched anyway (queries for PSP, FIELDS, SWEAP, ISOIS, WISPR CMADs) with no hit. (b) Data-center sites: SPDF /pub/data/psp/documents/ holds only the SDMP; SPDF /pub/documents/mission_PDMP_CMAD/ has no PSP entry (its senior_review_2020/ folder lists nothing); SPDF instrument folders hold a SWEAP data user guide (v1.3, January 2020) and an IS☉IS data user guide (Release 24, December 2025), neither a CMAD; the FIELDS SOC data page links release notes and component papers but no CMAD; the PSP Science Gateway is a JavaScript application with no reachable document listing; the Princeton ISOIS page returned HTTP 403. (c) Three general web searches (mission CMAD, instrument CMADs, senior-review/extended-mission CMAD) found no PSP CMAD. The SDMP was used as a mission-level source of names and roles but is not treated as a CMAD front page. Proceeded without CMAD evidence, so no candidate is Strong on current-team grounds.

instrument_coverage.notes: Reverse lookup in the SMWG clone (hpde/SMWG @ b8c8b803) found 25 Instrument records whose ObservatoryID is spase://SMWG/Observatory/ParkerSolarProbe, all under Instrument/ParkerSolarProbe/: the four suites (FIELDS, ISOIS, SWEAP, WISPR), 20 component records (FIELDS: DFB, FIELDS2/TDS, MAG, RFS/HFR, RFS/LFR, SCM, V1-V5; ISOIS: EPI-Lo, EPI-Hi/HET, LET1, LET2; SWEAP: SPC, SPAN-A, SPAN-B; WISPR: Inner and Outer Telescope), and an Ephemeris platform pseudo-instrument. The APL spacecraft page, the current and 2018 APL mission team pages, the NASA instruments page and the Observatory record's own Description all agree on four instrument suites: FIELDS, IS☉IS (ISOIS), SWEAP and WISPR. None is missing from SPASE. The 2018 team page also lists a fifth investigation, HeliOSPP (Heliospheric Origins with Solar Probe Plus, the theory and modeling investigation led by Marco Velli); it has no hardware, so it is not counted as a missing instrument. Component records carry only the suite PI, Nicola Fox (ProjectScientist) and a MetadataContact, so they add no new people; SWEAP component records still list Kasper and the WISPR telescope records still list Howard as PI (out of date, as in the suite records). The WISPR telescope records are stored as InnerTelescope.xml and OuterTelescope.xml but declare ResourceIDs .../WISPR/IT and .../WISPR/OT. The Ephemeris record has only MetadataContacts and no team.

notes: Mission paper selection confident: (Fox et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-015-0211-6) is linked from the Observatory record's own InformationURL, names the mission in its title, has 14 authors, was published online in November 2015 (Space Science Reviews 204, 2016), about three years before launch (a design-phase paper, inside the window), and has 1241 Crossref citations. A Semantic Scholar DOI lookup returns the same 14-author list. A Semantic Scholar keyword search surfaced only later science reviews (the strongest, a 2023 Space Science Reviews 'Four Years of Discoveries at Solar Cycle Minimum' review led by the Project Scientist, is a results review five years after launch). A Crossref search surfaced only 2010-2013 engineering conference papers (10.1109/aero.2013.6496957, 10.2514/6.2013-4879, 10.1016/j.actaastro.2010.06.007). SciX could not be queried (no API token; the web UI returned a human-verification page), so Crossref plus Semantic Scholar served as the literature cross-check.

Mission paper author order: backward scan finds a sorted suffix of 12 starting at author 3 (Bale ... Szabo), so the list is partially alphabetized with prefix = Fox, Velli (2); both are Strong. The 12 tail authors carry no position evidence; every one is corroborated independently (instrument Contacts and papers for Bale, Howard, Kasper and McComas; the mission team pages for Decker, Driesman, Kinnison, Raouafi and Szabo; the SDMP for Kinnison, Kusterer and Raouafi; a NASA Goddard biography for Lario; a 2017 APL release for Lockwood), so all 12 are Medium on this paper.

Instrument paper selection confident for all four: each is linked from its own Instrument record's InformationURL, names the instrument in its title, has 27-84 authors, appeared in the 2016 Space Science Reviews Solar Probe Plus volume (online 2014-2016, 2-4 years before launch) and has 221-802 Crossref citations. Semantic Scholar DOI lookups return the same author lists. No pending_instrument_runs entry was needed for any suite.

FIELDS (Bale et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-016-0244-5), n=84: a strict backward scan gives a sorted suffix of only 2, because two adjacent swaps (at positions 66-67 and 82-83) break an otherwise alphabetized run from author 10 to 84. Read strictly the list is not alphabetized; read tolerantly it is partially alphabetized with a 9-author prefix made of two separately sorted blocks (positions 1-4 and 5-9). Both readings give the same positions 1-3 (Bale, Goetz, Harvey), all Strong. Positions 4-5 (Turin, Bonnell) are excluded as instrument-team depth.

SWEAP (Kasper et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-015-0206-3), n=79: a strict backward scan gives a sorted suffix of 22 from author 58, but authors 2-79 are plainly alphabetized with three small misorderings (adjacent pairs at positions 32-33, 53-54 and 57-58). Following the near-sorted rule, which errs against awarding position evidence, the list is treated as partially alphabetized with prefix = Kasper alone. Abiad and Austin at positions 2-3 got no position evidence and are excluded.

ISOIS (McComas et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-014-0059-1), n=51: with the name particle kept (the 'von' surname at position 48 sorted under V) the sorted suffix is 50, from author 2 to the end, so the list is partially alphabetized with prefix = McComas alone. Alexander and Angold at positions 2-3 got no position evidence. (If the particle is stripped, a single inversion appears at positions 47-48; the conclusion is the same.)

WISPR (Vourlidas et al. 2016, 10.1007/s11214-014-0114-y), n=27: 13 adjacent inversions, not alphabetized. Positions 1-3 are Vourlidas, Howard, Plunkett (Strong); positions 4-5 (Korendyke, Thernisien) are excluded as instrument-team depth.

Instrument-paper authors at position 6 and beyond are not listed individually (FIELDS 84, SWEAP 79, ISOIS 51 and WISPR 27 authors), because they carry no position-based evidence on any run. Exceptions: someone is listed when they were evaluated on another source (for example the SOC leads and the current WISPR and SWEAP PIs).

Out-of-date Contacts: the current APL mission team page (2026) and spacecraft page name Michael Stevens (CfA) as SWEAP PI and Mark Linton (NRL) as WISPR PI, while the SWEAP and WISPR Instrument records (and their component records) still list Justin Kasper and Russell Howard. The September 2021 SDMP already names Linton for WISPR but still Kasper for SWEAP, so the WISPR change predates September 2021 and the SWEAP change came after it. Kasper and Howard are therefore FormerPI, and Stevens and Linton are InstrumentLead. Each suite has exactly one InstrumentLead: FIELDS Bale, ISOIS McComas, SWEAP Stevens, WISPR Linton.

Conflicting provider pages: the NASA instruments page still says the SWEAP PI is Justin Kasper (University of Michigan) and the WISPR PI is Russell Howard, and the SWEAP team page lists 'Justin Kasper (Principal Investigator)' under the University of Michigan while also stating that SWEAP is led by the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory. These look like un-updated launch-era text; the APL mission-operator pages were taken as the current authority.

Stevens and Linton are Medium, not Strong: on an Observatory record the Strong provider-PI criterion refers to the mission PI, so an instrument PI named on the mission's team page counts as 'named on the provider's team page' (Medium). Their inclusion does not depend on this choice.

Mission team page role gate (judgment call): the qualifying-role rule for Contacts was applied to the APL mission team pages and the SDMP approval pages. People named there only in management, engineering or outreach roles (Program Executive, Program/Project Manager, systems engineers, mission operations, public affairs) are excluded, and those pages serve only to corroborate people who co-authored the mission overview paper. Arik Posner is included because Program Scientist is a qualifying role. A reviewer who wants every team-page name treated as Medium, or who wants HQ program officials kept off the DOI, should revisit Posner and the 27 excluded management entries.

Raouafi's role: the Observatory record Contacts list him as PrincipalInvestigator, but Parker Solar Probe is an APL-implemented Living With a Star mission. Its team pages list no mission-level PI and name him Project Scientist, as does the 2021 SDMP, so ProjectScientist is recorded and PrincipalInvestigator is not. The Observatory Contact role likely needs correcting.

Fox's role: she was the original Project Scientist (Observatory and all component Contacts; 2018 team page), but the current page and the 2021 SDMP name Raouafi. SPASE has no former-project-scientist role, so ProjectScientist is kept for Fox, with a role_evidence source stating it is the founding-generation role. The Observatory will therefore carry two ProjectScientist contacts; the reviewer should confirm this is the intended representation.

Roles with no qualifying SPASE equivalent, recorded as Author only: Velli (HeliOSPP PI / theory investigation lead at launch), Decker (Deputy Project Scientist; his Observatory Contact role 'Scientist' is non-qualifying), Szabo (NASA Mission Scientist) and Lario (Deputy Mission Scientist).

Sources used only for PI/role checks, with their names not evaluated individually: the SWEAP team page's full Co-Investigator list, the SDMP revision log (document editors, which is not authorship evidence), and the preparers named on the ISOIS data user guide (ISOIS SOC staff). All are instrument-team depth for the relevant Instrument-record runs.

Component-level description papers (DFB 10.1002/2016JA022344; RFS 10.1002/2016JA023345, linked from the FIELDS data page) were not harvested on this Observatory run; they are listed in pending_instrument_runs for the component records. No component papers were looked up for the SWEAP, ISOIS or WISPR components or the other FIELDS components.

Registry issues for curators: (1) the James.M.Weygand Person record's PersonName reads 'Robert M. Candey'; (2) duplicate Person records exist for Michael.L.Stevens and Michael.Louis.Stevens. Michael.L.Stevens is used here because other records (Repository/HU/CfA, DSCOVR Faraday Cup) reference it; (3) the Simon.Plunkett Person record has no PersonName and gives NASA Headquarters, and it was matched to the WISPR co-author by name; (4) the Observatory InformationURL 'Parker Solar Probe Mission Web Page, JPL' points to the JHU/APL site, not JPL; (5) the Instrument records' NASA instruments link (https://www.nasa.gov/content/goddard/parker-solar-probe-instruments/) returns HTTP 404; (6) the current APL team page lists 'Project Scientist' twice (Nour Raouafi and Nour Rawafi, a spelling variant of the same person).

Name forms: Crossref gives Fox as 'Fox, N. J.' on the mission paper and 'Fox, Nichola' on the SWEAP paper; the SMWG Person record is Nicola J. Fox. Kinnison appears as 'Kinnison, J.' and 'Jim Kinnison'; Kusterer as 'Kusterer, M.' and 'Martha B. Kusterer' (SDMP).

ORCID and affiliation were captured opportunistically. Crossref carries no affiliations for any of the five papers and an ORCID only for Kasper; the other ORCIDs (Howard, Vourlidas, Schwadron) come from SMWG Person records. Affiliations come from Person records, the team pages, the SDMP and staff biographies. Kusterer's affiliation is left null because no fetched source states it.
Crossref 'issued' dates are the online-first dates (2014-2015); citations use 2016, the print year of Space Science Reviews volume 204, which carries all five papers.
